title: Meet D-Rex, a Giant Fungus
summary:
Scientists exploring forests in Yunnan, China, found a giant fungus nicknamed D-rex. Its upright parts can grow 50 cm (20 inches) tall and weigh up to 2.2 kg (4.9 pounds), the largest known fruiting bodies in the group called Ascomycota.

The species, Dianjunus rex, is named for its size and the ancient Dian kingdom. It is different enough to need a new genus and a whole new family, Dianjunaceae.

The team found it in forests near Damaidi and Yipinglang, and rainforest near Nanbang, spotting whitish stromata on the roots of Chinese cork oak trees.

Unlike familiar mushrooms, ascomycetes make spores inside tiny sac-like structures.

Using a molecular clock, scientists compared its DNA with hundreds of fungi. The family seems to have appeared about 65 million years ago, roughly one million years after the mass extinction that wiped out the non-avian dinosaurs.

Dr Indunil C Senanayake, of the Kunming Institute of Botany, said the timing raises a possibility: after the extinction, forests changed, and large amounts of dead plant material became available, which may have created new chances for wood-breaking fungi.
why_it_matters: It shows that even in forests, scientists can still find huge living things nobody knew about, which is why exploring nature carefully matters.
